[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#purpose-statement]

### Purpose Statement

This standard defines the mandatory naming conventions for every artifact in the Golden Path Catalog — path identifiers, variant suffixes, template directory paths, verification contracts, changelogs, machine-readable index fields, and conformance check identifiers. It provides a single authoritative reference so that Platform Engineering contributors, catalog tooling, and the Intent-to-Infrastructure pipeline all apply the same conventions without triangulating across multiple pattern documents.
page_texts.6:
[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#scope]

### Scope

**In Scope:**

- Golden Path identifiers (`GP-{NNN}`) and variant suffixes (`GP-{NNN}-{DESCRIPTOR}`)
- Catalog filesystem layout: template directories, verification contracts, changelogs, and path specification directories under `catalog/`
- Machine-readable `catalog/index.yaml` field values: `id`, `name`, `workload_class`, `template_path`, `verification_contract`, `changelog`, `status`, `version`
- Language and platform variant qualifiers on scaffold template directories
- Conformance check identifiers declared in Verification Contracts and scaffold validation files

**Out of Scope:**

- Service repository naming (see STD-APP-SVC-001 when published)
- Kubernetes resource and namespace naming
- Terraform module naming
- Kafka topic naming (see [STD-INF-EVT-001](../information/event-driven/STD-INF-EVT-001-kafka-topic-design-naming.md))
- GitHub repository naming
- Pipeline and workflow naming
page_texts.7:
[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#compliance-level]

### Compliance Level

**Mandatory.** All Platform Engineering contributors and all catalog tooling must conform to this standard. Non-conformant path IDs, field values, or filesystem paths are blocked from merge by the catalog publish CI gate.
page_texts.8:
[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#business-rationale]

### Business Rationale

The Golden Path Catalog is consumed by both human contributors and machine tooling — including the Golden Path Selector in the Intent-to-Infrastructure pipeline (PTN-TEC-AI-001) and the Conformance Gate CI step (PTN-GOV-AI-003). Inconsistent naming in catalog artifacts causes:

- **Pipeline failures**: The Golden Path Selector matches intent documents to catalog entries via the `workload_class` field. A case mismatch (`hipaa-rest-microservice` vs. `HIPAA-REST-MICROSERVICE`) causes a miss and falls back to an incorrect or no path selection.
- **Tooling drift**: Multiple teams independently invent qualifiers (e.g., `gp-001-csharp` vs. `gp-001-dotnet`) for the same stack, producing duplicate templates that cannot be shared.
- **Governance risk**: Non-sequential or reused path IDs make it impossible to determine the canonical catalog size, detect gaps, or automate deprecation notices.

---
page_texts.10:
[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#mandatory-requirements]

### Mandatory Requirements

- **REQ-001**: All base path IDs must use the format `GP-{NNN}` where `GP` is all-uppercase and `{NNN}` is a three-digit zero-padded sequential integer (e.g., `GP-001`, `GP-042`).
- **REQ-002**: Path IDs are immutable after assignment. Superseded paths must be deprecated; the successor receives a new ID.
- **REQ-003**: Variant path IDs must use the format `GP-{NNN}-{DESCRIPTOR}` where `{DESCRIPTOR}` is SCREAMING-KEBAB-CASE (e.g., `GP-001-MT`, `GP-001-FHIR`).
- **REQ-004**: Scaffold template directories must follow `catalog/templates/{path-id-lowercase}-{language}/` using a registered language qualifier from the approved list in §Technical Specifications.
- **REQ-005**: The `workload_class` field in `catalog/index.yaml` must be `lowercase-kebab-case`.
- **REQ-006**: The `id` field in `catalog/index.yaml` must match the registered path ID exactly, including uppercase `GP` prefix.
- **REQ-007**: Verification contract filenames must follow `{PATH-ID-UPPERCASE}-verification-contract.yaml`.
- **REQ-008**: Changelog filenames must follow `{PATH-ID-UPPERCASE}.md`.
- **REQ-009**: Conformance check identifiers must use the format `SC-{NNN}`, numbered sequentially within each path's Verification Contract.
- **REQ-010**: New language qualifiers must be registered in the approved list in §Technical Specifications before first use in any template directory.
page_texts.11:
[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#recommended-practices]

### Recommended Practices

- **REC-001**: Assign path IDs sequentially with no deliberate gaps. Gaps arise only from retired paths and must be documented in the changelog for that ID.
- **REC-002**: Keep variant descriptors to one or two tokens (e.g., `MT`, `FHIR`) unless three are genuinely necessary to distinguish the variant (e.g., `EXT-VENDOR-INTEGRATION`).
- **REC-003**: Author one Verification Contract per base path ID covering all language variants; use per-check file path conditions to handle language differences rather than duplicating the contract.
- **REC-004**: Use `status: 'experimental'` for any path without full ARB approval. Do not publish `status: 'active'` without a `last_arb_review` date populated.
- **REC-005**: Place the `workload_class` value in the Golden Path Proposal PR description so Selector matching can be validated before merge.
page_texts.12:
[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#prohibited-practices]

### Prohibited Practices

- **PRO-001**: Do not use lowercase for the `GP` prefix in any path ID (`gp-001` is invalid in all contexts).
- **PRO-002**: Do not use underscores in path IDs, variant descriptors, or `workload_class` values (`GP-001_MT`, `hipaa_rest_microservice` are invalid).
- **PRO-003**: Do not omit the language qualifier from template directory names once a path has more than one approved stack. A bare `catalog/templates/gp-001/` is not permitted after a second language variant is added.
- **PRO-004**: Do not mix casing conventions within a single `index.yaml` entry.
- **PRO-005**: Do not reuse a retired path ID. Once retired, an ID is permanently reserved as a tombstone.
- **PRO-006**: Do not invent per-path language qualifiers. Only qualifiers from the approved list may be used.
page_texts.13:
[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#exceptions-process]

### Exceptions Process

1. **Machine-consumed fields (REQ-001 through REQ-009)**: No exceptions are permitted. These fields are validated programmatically; exceptions cannot be honored at runtime — the pipeline will fail until the field is corrected.
2. **Human-readable `name` field**: Exceptions to Title Case rules may be requested where product brand naming conflicts. The Platform Engineering lead approves via PR comment.
3. **New language qualifiers (REQ-010)**: Propose via a PR that adds the qualifier to the approved list in §Technical Specifications (the "qualifier PR"). Per the Architecture Review Board's standards-mandated path, the qualifier PR must complete Security Domain Review before ARB approval is requested; ARB approval is required before the qualifier PR is merged.
4. All approved exceptions must be recorded in the Approved Exceptions Log in §Compliance and Governance within 5 business days.

---
page_texts.15:
[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#design-principles]

### Design Principles

- **Machine-first where it matters**: Fields consumed by the catalog API, the Golden Path Selector, and the Conformance Gate use machine-safe formats (lowercase-kebab, SCREAMING-KEBAB, sequential integers) to eliminate parsing ambiguity.
- **Human-readable where it matters**: Display names and document titles use natural Title Case so developers can read catalog entries without decoding identifiers.
- **One format per field**: Each catalog field has exactly one canonical case and character set; tooling must validate and reject non-conformant values at catalog publish time.
- **Additive, not destructive**: Variant path IDs (`GP-NNN-DESCRIPTOR`) and language qualifiers (`-dotnet`, `-java`, `-python`) extend the base path ID without replacing it, preserving the base as the authoritative cross-language identity.
page_texts.16:
[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#architecture-constraints]

### Architecture Constraints

- **No cross-path ID sharing**: Two distinct workload archetypes may not share a path ID, even temporarily. Each workload class receives its own sequential ID from first experimental to active.
- **Immutable IDs**: A path ID is immutable after its first catalog entry is merged. Superseded paths are deprecated; the successor receives a new ID. This ensures deprecation automation can reliably track all instances of a path in service repositories.
- **Filesystem case sensitivity**: The catalog repository is hosted on a Linux runner. Template directory names and all paths under `catalog/` are case-sensitive. A path-id must be consistently lowercase in filesystem paths and consistently uppercase in `index.yaml` ID and filename fields — mixing causes CI failures on Linux runners even if they appear to work locally on macOS or Windows.
- **No runtime exceptions for machine fields**: Fields consumed by the Golden Path Selector (`workload_class`), Conformance Gate (`id`, check IDs), and catalog API (`status`, `version`) must be format-valid at CI time. There is no runtime override mechanism.

---
page_texts.18:
[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#21-base-path-id]

### 2.1 Base Path ID

The path identifier is the primary key for a Golden Path across all catalog artifacts.

**Format:** `GP-{NNN}`

| Token | Description |
|---|---|
| `GP` | Fixed prefix — stands for Golden Path |
| `-` | Literal hyphen separator |
| `{NNN}` | Three-digit zero-padded sequential integer assigned at catalog registration |

**Rules:**

- Sequential assignment only — no gaps, no reuse of retired IDs.
- Zero-padded to three digits: `GP-001`, `GP-009`, `GP-010`, `GP-099`, `GP-100`.
- All-uppercase prefix `GP` — never lowercase `gp-` in the path ID itself.
- The ID is immutable after assignment. If a path is fundamentally replaced, the successor path receives a new ID and the original is deprecated.

**Valid examples:** `GP-001`, `GP-007`, `GP-042`
**Invalid examples:** `GP-1`, `gp-001`, `GP001`, `GOLDEN-PATH-001`
page_texts.19:
[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#22-variant-suffix]

### 2.2 Variant Suffix

When a path shares the same core workload class as a base path but diverges in compliance tier, integration topology, or deployment target, it receives a variant suffix rather than a new sequential ID tier.

**Format:** `GP-{NNN}-{DESCRIPTOR}`

| Token | Description |
|---|---|
| `GP-{NNN}` | Base path ID (see §2.1) |
| `-` | Literal hyphen separator |
| `{DESCRIPTOR}` | One- to three-word SCREAMING-KEBAB-CASE descriptor identifying the axis of divergence |

**Rules:**

- `{DESCRIPTOR}` must be SCREAMING-KEBAB-CASE: all uppercase, hyphens as word separators, no underscores or spaces.
- Descriptor must reflect the divergence axis, not the technology stack (technology is encoded in the template folder —see §3.1).
- Maximum three tokens in the descriptor to maintain readability.

**Valid examples:** `GP-001-MT`, `GP-001-FHIR`, `GP-001-MARSE`, `GP-003-HIPAA`, `GP-001-EXT-VENDOR-INTEGRATION`
**Invalid examples:** `gp-001-mt`, `GP-001_MT`, `GP-001-multi-tenant`
page_texts.20:
[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#23-proposing-a-new-path-id]

### 2.3 Proposing a New Path ID

A new path ID is assigned at the time the Golden Path Proposal PR is merged (see PTN-GOV-AI-001). The PR template field **Proposed Path ID** must follow the `GP-{NNN}` format. The catalog maintainer confirms there is no ID collision before merge.

---
page_texts.21:
[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#30-catalog-artifact-paths]

## 3.0 Catalog Artifact Paths

These are the filesystem paths under which all catalog artifacts must be stored.
page_texts.22:
[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#31-scaffold-template-directory]

### 3.1 Scaffold Template Directory

**Format:** `catalog/templates/{path-id}-{language}/`

| Token | Description |
|---|---|
| `{path-id}` | Base path ID or variant suffix ID, **lowercased** (e.g., `gp-001`, `gp-001-mt`) |
| `-` | Literal hyphen separator |
| `{language}` | Lowercase technology stack identifier (see §3.1.1) |

A separate directory is required for each approved technology stack variant. Both directories share the same Verification Contract.

**Examples:**

```
catalog/templates/gp-001-dotnet/
catalog/templates/gp-001-java/
catalog/templates/gp-001-python/
catalog/templates/gp-001-mt-dotnet/
```

**Invalid examples:**

```
catalog/templates/GP-001-dotnet/       ← uppercase path ID
catalog/templates/gp001-dotnet/        ← missing hyphen between GP and NNN
catalog/templates/gp-001/              ← missing language qualifier (multi-stack paths)
```
page_texts.23:
[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#311-approved-language-qualifiers]

#### 3.1.1 Approved Language Qualifiers

| Language / Framework | Qualifier |
|---|---|
| .NET (any version) | `dotnet` |
| Java / Spring Boot | `java` |
| Python / FastAPI | `python` |
| Node.js / TypeScript | `node` |
| React (MFE) | `react` |

New qualifiers must be registered in this table before use. Do not invent qualifiers per-path.
page_texts.24:
[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#32-verification-contract]

### 3.2 Verification Contract

**Format:** `catalog/verification-contracts/{path-id}-verification-contract.yaml`

| Token | Description |
|---|---|
| `{path-id}` | Base path ID, **uppercase as registered** (e.g., `GP-001`) |

One Verification Contract per path ID. Language variants share a single contract; language-specific file path differences are handled within the contract using per-check `file_exists` paths or check conditions.

**Examples:**

```
catalog/verification-contracts/GP-001-verification-contract.yaml
catalog/verification-contracts/GP-001-MT-verification-contract.yaml
catalog/verification-contracts/GP-007-verification-contract.yaml
```
page_texts.25:
[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#33-changelog]

### 3.3 Changelog

**Format:** `catalog/changelogs/{path-id}.md`

| Token | Description |
|---|---|
| `{path-id}` | Base path ID, **uppercase as registered** (e.g., `GP-001`) |

**Examples:**

```
catalog/changelogs/GP-001.md
catalog/changelogs/GP-001-MT.md
```
page_texts.26:
[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#34-path-specification-directory]

### 3.4 Path Specification Directory

**Format:** `catalog/paths/{path-id}/`

Path specifications include `constraints.md` and any supplementary path governance documents.

**Examples:**

```
catalog/paths/GP-001/constraints.md
catalog/paths/GP-001-MT/constraints.md
```
page_texts.27:
[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#35-scaffold-validation-file]

### 3.5 Scaffold Validation File

Each scaffold template directory must contain a `scaffold-validation.yaml` at its root.

**Format:** `catalog/templates/{path-id}-{language}/scaffold-validation.yaml`

This is a fixed filename. Do not vary it per path or language.
page_texts.28:
[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#36-summary-of-catalog-filesystem-layout]

### 3.6 Summary of Catalog Filesystem Layout

```
catalog/
├── index.yaml                                          ← Machine-readable catalog index
├── paths/
│   ├── GP-001/
│   │   └── constraints.md
│   └── GP-001-MT/
│       └── constraints.md
├── templates/
│   ├── gp-001-dotnet/                                  ← {path-id lowercase}-{language}
│   │   ├── scaffold-validation.yaml
│   │   └── template.json
│   └── gp-001-java/
│       ├── scaffold-validation.yaml
│       └── template.json
├── verification-contracts/
│   ├── GP-001-verification-contract.yaml               ← {path-id uppercase}-verification-contract.yaml
│   └── GP-001-MT-verification-contract.yaml
└── changelogs/
    ├── GP-001.md                                       ← {path-id uppercase}.md
    └── GP-001-MT.md
```

---
page_texts.29:
[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#40-index-fields]

## 4.0 Index Fields

These rules apply to every entry in `catalog/index.yaml`. All fields are machine-read by the catalog API and the Golden Path Selector in the Intent-to-Infrastructure pipeline.
page_texts.30:
[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#41-id]

### 4.1 `id`

**Format:** `GP-{NNN}` or `GP-{NNN}-{DESCRIPTOR}` (see §2.1–§2.2)
**Case:** SCREAMING-KEBAB: uppercase `GP`, uppercase `DESCRIPTOR`
**Type:** string, quoted in YAML

```yaml
id: 'GP-001'
id: 'GP-001-MT'
```
page_texts.31:
[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#42-name]

### 4.2 `name`

The human-readable display name for the path.

**Format:** Title Case natural language — capitalize each significant word; prepositions and articles lowercase unless first word.
**Type:** string, quoted in YAML

```yaml
name: 'HIPAA REST Microservice on AKS'
name: 'HIPAA Multi-Tenant REST Microservice on AKS'
name: 'Event-Driven Consumer Service'
```
page_texts.32:
[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#43-workloadclass]

### 4.3 `workload_class`

The workload class identifies the architectural workload archetype. It is the primary matching key used by the Golden Path Selector when resolving an intent document to a catalog entry.

**Format:** `lowercase-kebab-case` — all lowercase, hyphens as word separators, no underscores or spaces.
**Type:** string, quoted in YAML

```yaml
workload_class: 'hipaa-rest-microservice'
workload_class: 'hipaa-rest-microservice-mt'
workload_class: 'event-driven-consumer'
workload_class: 'scheduled-batch-job'
```

> **Note on generation manifests:** The `golden_path_selected` field in the Intent-to-Infrastructure generation manifest (produced by PTN-TEC-AI-001) uses a different format — `SCREAMING-KEBAB-CASE-V{N}` — because it is a composite key embedding the path ID, workload class, and catalog version. That field is a pipeline output artifact; it is not the same as the `workload_class` field in `index.yaml`. Do not conflate the two.
page_texts.33:
[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#44-templatepath]

### 4.4 `template_path`

**Format:** `catalog/templates/{path-id-lowercase}-{language}/`
**Type:** string, quoted in YAML

When a path has multiple language variants, list them as a YAML sequence:

```yaml
# Single language
template_path: 'catalog/templates/gp-001-dotnet/'

# Multiple languages
template_paths:
  - 'catalog/templates/gp-001-dotnet/'
  - 'catalog/templates/gp-001-java/'
```
page_texts.36:
[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#47-version]

### 4.7 `version`

**Format:** Semantic versioning — `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`

- `MAJOR` — breaking change to scaffold contract or Verification Contract structure
- `MINOR` — additive change (new approved stack, new optional control stub)
- `PATCH` — dependency update, bug fix, documentation correction

```yaml
version: '1.0.0'
version: '1.2.0'
```
page_texts.37:
[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#48-status]

### 4.8 `status`

**Format:** One of four fixed lowercase values (no SCREAMING-KEBAB here).

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `experimental` | Piloting; ARB review pending; not a valid AI generation target |
| `active` | Full ARB approval; valid generation target |
| `deprecated` | Superseded; migration window open; blocked from new generation |
| `retired` | Migration window closed; removed from active index |

```yaml
status: 'experimental'
status: 'active'
```

---
page_texts.38:
[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#50-conformance-check-identifiers]

## 5.0 Conformance Check Identifiers

Conformance check IDs appear in `scaffold-validation.yaml` and Verification Contract files.

**Format:** `SC-{NNN}`

| Token | Description |
|---|---|
| `SC` | Fixed prefix — stands for Structural Check |
| `-` | Literal hyphen separator |
| `{NNN}` | Three-digit zero-padded sequential integer scoped within the path |

**Rules:**

- Numbering is path-scoped, not catalog-global. Two paths may each have `SC-001`; they do not conflict.
- Sequential within a path's Verification Contract. No gaps unless a check is formally removed.
- All-uppercase prefix `SC` — never lowercase.

**Examples:** `SC-001`, `SC-017`

[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#approved-language-qualifiers]

| Java / Spring Boot | `java` | `catalog/templates/gp-001-java/` |
| Python / FastAPI | `python` | `catalog/templates/gp-001-python/` |
| Node.js / TypeScript | `node` | `catalog/templates/gp-001-node/` |

page_texts.41:
[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#status-enum-values]

#### Status Enum Values

The `status` field accepts exactly these four lowercase values:

| Value | Meaning | AI Generation Target? |
|---|---|---|
| `experimental` | Piloting; ARB review pending | No |
| `active` | Full ARB approval obtained | Yes |
| `deprecated` | Superseded; migration window open | No — blocked |
| `retired` | Migration window closed; removed from active index | No |
page_texts.43:
[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#complete-naming-reference]

#### Complete Naming Reference

| Artifact | Format | Case Rule | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| Base Path ID | `GP-{NNN}` | `GP` uppercase, NNN zero-padded | `GP-001` |
| Variant Path ID | `GP-{NNN}-{DESCRIPTOR}` | SCREAMING-KEBAB | `GP-001-MT`, `GP-001-FHIR` |
| Template directory | `catalog/templates/{path-id}-{language}/` | path-id **lowercase**, language lowercase | `catalog/templates/gp-001-dotnet/` |
| Verification contract filename | `{PATH-ID}-verification-contract.yaml` | path-id **uppercase** | `GP-001-verification-contract.yaml` |
| Changelog filename | `{PATH-ID}.md` | path-id **uppercase** | `GP-001.md` |
| Path spec directory | `catalog/paths/{PATH-ID}/` | path-id **uppercase** | `catalog/paths/GP-001/` |
| `id` field | `GP-{NNN}` | SCREAMING-KEBAB | `'GP-001'` |
| `name` field | Natural language | Title Case | `'HIPAA REST Microservice on AKS'` |
| `workload_class` field | Kebab descriptors | **lowercase-kebab** | `'hipaa-rest-microservice'` |
| `template_path` field | Filesystem path | path-id **lowercase** | `'catalog/templates/gp-001-dotnet/'` |
| `verification_contract` field | Filesystem path | path-id **uppercase** | `'catalog/verification-contracts/GP-001-verification-contract.yaml'` |
| `changelog` field | Filesystem path | path-id **uppercase** | `'catalog/changelogs/GP-001.md'` |
| `status` field | Fixed enum | **all lowercase** | `'active'` |
| Conformance check ID | `SC-{NNN}` | `SC` uppercase, NNN zero-padded | `SC-001` |
| Language qualifier | Single descriptor | **all lowercase** | `dotnet`, `java`, `python` |
page_texts.44:
[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#conformant-catalogindexyaml-entry]

#### Conformant `catalog/index.yaml` Entry

```yaml
# catalog/index.yaml
- id: 'GP-001'                                    # SCREAMING-KEBAB, matches registered path ID
  name: 'HIPAA REST Microservice on AKS'          # Title Case natural language
  status: 'active'                                # lowercase fixed enum
  version: '1.2.0'                               # semantic versioning
  workload_class: 'hipaa-rest-microservice'       # lowercase-kebab — Golden Path Selector key
```

[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#phase-1-catalog-entry-authoring]

#### Phase 1: Catalog Entry Authoring

1. Obtain the next available sequential path ID from the catalog maintainer (check `catalog/index.yaml` preamble comment for current maximum).
2. Author `catalog/paths/{PATH-ID}/constraints.md` using the uppercase path ID.
3. Draft the `catalog/index.yaml` entry following the Configuration Specifications above. Validate `workload_class` is lowercase-kebab and `id` matches the registered path ID exactly.
4. Author the Verification Contract at `catalog/verification-contracts/{PATH-ID}-verification-contract.yaml`. Assign `SC-{NNN}` IDs sequentially starting at `SC-001`.
page_texts.49:
[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#phase-2-scaffold-template-authoring]

#### Phase 2: Scaffold Template Authoring

1. Create one template directory per approved technology stack: `catalog/templates/{path-id-lowercase}-{language}/`. Use only qualifiers from the approved language qualifier table.
2. Place `scaffold-validation.yaml` at the root of each template directory. This filename is fixed — do not vary it per path or language.
3. Verify that the `template_paths` values in `catalog/index.yaml` match the directories created — path-id must be lowercased and language qualifier exact.
page_texts.50:
[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#phase-3-pre-merge-validation]

#### Phase 3: Pre-Merge Validation

1. Run `conformance-check --validate-catalog catalog/index.yaml` to verify all field formats before opening a PR.
2. Run `conformance-check --validate-scaffold catalog/templates/{path-id}-{language}/` for each template directory.
3. Cross-check all filesystem artifact paths in the PR diff to confirm uppercase/lowercase rules are applied as specified in §Technical Specifications.

[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#validation-criteria]

### Validation Criteria

| Validation Area | Criteria | Verification Method | Evidence Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| Path ID format | Matches `GP-{NNN}` or `GP-{NNN}-{DESCRIPTOR}`, uppercase, zero-padded | `conformance-check` CI gate | Gate pass in PR check |
| `workload_class` case | All lowercase, hyphen-separated, no underscores or spaces | `conformance-check` CI gate | Gate pass in PR check |
| Template directory name | `{path-id-lowercase}-{language}/`, registered qualifier only | PR reviewer check + CI | PR approval + gate pass |
| Verification contract filename | `{PATH-ID-UPPERCASE}-verification-contract.yaml` | PR reviewer check | PR approval |
| Changelog filename | `{PATH-ID-UPPERCASE}.md` | PR reviewer check | PR approval |
| Conformance check IDs | `SC-{NNN}`, sequential within path, no gaps | PR reviewer check | PR approval |
| Language qualifier | Registered in approved list | PR reviewer check | PR approval + if new: ARB approval |
page_texts.52:
[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#testing-requirements]

### Testing Requirements

- **Conformance Gate**: All `catalog/index.yaml` entries must pass `conformance-check --validate-catalog` before merge. This is a blocking automated check.
- **Scaffold Validation**: All scaffold template directories must pass `conformance-check --validate-scaffold` before merge. This is a blocking automated check.
- **ID Collision Test**: The CI gate must verify no two active or experimental entries share the same `id` or `workload_class` value.
- **Retired ID Tombstone Test**: The CI gate must verify no new entry reuses a path ID present in the catalog tombstone list.
page_texts.53:
[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#documentation-requirements]

### Documentation Requirements

- **Catalog index entry**: Every path must have a complete `catalog/index.yaml` entry meeting all field requirements before being considered `experimental`.
- **Constraints document**: `catalog/paths/{PATH-ID}/constraints.md` must be present for all paths at `experimental` or higher status.
- **Changelog**: `catalog/changelogs/{PATH-ID}.md` must be created at the same time as the initial `index.yaml` entry and updated with each version bump.
- **Standard update for new qualifiers**: If a new language qualifier is introduced, the approved qualifier table in this standard must be updated in the same PR that adds the qualifier.

page_texts.56:
[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#assessment-criteria]

#### Assessment Criteria

- **Criterion 1 — Field format compliance**: All `index.yaml` fields conform to the case and format rules in §Technical Specifications. Target: zero field format violations across all catalog entries.
- **Criterion 2 — Filesystem path compliance**: All artifact paths under `catalog/` conform to the naming rules. Target: zero path non-conformances detected during PR review.
- **Criterion 3 — Qualifier registration compliance**: No template directory uses an unregistered language qualifier. Target: all qualifiers present in template directory names appear in the approved list.
page_texts.57:
[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#assessment-process]

#### Assessment Process

1. **Continuous** — The `conformance-check` CI gate runs on every PR modifying any file under `catalog/`. Results are recorded in the PR check log.
2. **Quarterly** — The Platform Engineering catalog maintainer runs a full scan of all template directory names and `index.yaml` entries to detect drift that bypassed CI (e.g., direct commits to main). Findings are filed as issues and remediated within 30 days.
3. **At each ARB review** — ARB reviewers confirm the path ID and `workload_class` values for the path under review before ARB approval is recorded.
page_texts.58:
[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#monitoring-requirements]

### Monitoring Requirements

- **Continuous Monitoring**: The catalog publish CI gate validates all `index.yaml` field formats on every PR. Failures surface as blocking PR checks.
- **Periodic Reviews**: Quarterly catalog scan per Assessment Process above. Results reported to Platform Engineering lead.
- **Incident Reporting**: Any naming non-conformance discovered post-merge (e.g., production pipeline failure caused by a `workload_class` mismatch) must be filed as a P2 platform incident, remediated within 24 hours, and root-cause documented in the catalog maintainer's incident log.
- **Metrics Collection**: Track `% of catalog index entries passing conformance-check on first PR submission` as a leading indicator of standard adoption.
page_texts.60:
[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#exception-categories]

#### Exception Categories

- **Temporary Exceptions**: Not applicable for machine-consumed fields (REQ-001 through REQ-009). No temporary exception mechanism exists for fields validated programmatically — the pipeline fails until the field is corrected.
- **Permanent Exceptions**: Available only for the human-readable `name` field where brand or product naming conflicts with Title Case rules. Requires Platform Engineering lead approval.
- **Emergency Exceptions**: In the event of a production pipeline outage caused by a `workload_class` mismatch, the remediation path is correction of the non-conformant value, not an exception grant. The CI gate must be restored before the next catalog publish.
page_texts.61:
[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#exception-management-process]

#### Exception Management Process

1. Submit an exception request as a comment on the PR where the non-conformance exists, tagging the Platform Engineering lead.
2. Describe the conflict: which requirement, which field, and why the standard value cannot be used.
3. For `name` field exceptions: Platform Engineering lead approves via PR comment. No ARB involvement required.
4. For new language qualifiers (REQ-010): Open a separate PR proposing the addition to this standard with justification. Per the [Architecture Review Board's standards-mandated path](../../governance/governing-bodies/architecture-review-board.md#when-an-arb-input-form-is-required), the PR must complete Security Domain Review before ARB approval is requested; ARB approval is required before the qualifier PR is merged.
5. Record all approved exceptions in the table below.

### Governance Oversight

- **Standards Owner (Platform Engineering — Catalog Maintainer)**: Assigns new path IDs, enforces naming at PR merge, updates this standard when new qualifiers are registered or exceptions are approved.
- **Compliance Manager (Platform Engineering Lead)**: Monitors quarterly assessment results, approves `name` field exceptions, escalates repeated violations.
- **Governance Body (Architecture Review Board)**: Approves new language qualifiers, approves permanent exceptions, reviews this standard at each annual review.
- **Subject Matter Experts**: Golden Path authors from contributing teams are responsible for applying this standard in their proposals. The PR template (PTN-GOV-AI-001) includes a naming conformance checklist item.

[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#example-1-authoring-a-new-base-path-gp-008]

#### Example 1: Authoring a New Base Path (GP-008)

**Context:** Platform Engineering is proposing GP-008 (Scheduled Batch Job on AKS, .NET only) as a new Golden Path.

**Implementation:**

- Path ID assigned: `GP-008` (next available after `GP-007`)
- `workload_class`: `scheduled-batch-job` (lowercase-kebab)
- Template directory: `catalog/templates/gp-008-dotnet/` (`gp-008` lowercased, `dotnet` from approved list)
- Verification contract: `catalog/verification-contracts/GP-008-verification-contract.yaml` (`GP-008` uppercased)

**Compliance Evidence:** `conformance-check` CI gate passes. PR reviewers confirmed all filesystem paths in the diff match §Technical Specifications.

**Lessons Learned:** Setting `status: 'experimental'` from day one prevents the Golden Path Selector from routing production intent documents to an unreviewed path.
page_texts.67:
[standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#example-2-adding-a-variant-gp-001-fhir]

#### Example 2: Adding a Variant (GP-001-FHIR)

**Context:** A FHIR/SMART-on-FHIR API workload diverges from GP-001 in compliance tier (adds PTN-SEC-API-009 controls) but shares the same base scaffold structure.

**Implementation:**

- Variant ID: `GP-001-FHIR` (base `GP-001`, descriptor `FHIR` — single SCREAMING-KEBAB token)
- `workload_class`: `hipaa-fhir-api` — a **new distinct** lowercase-kebab value; not a suffix of the base `workload_class` because the Selector uses it as a unique key
- Template directory: `catalog/templates/gp-001-fhir-dotnet/`
- Verification contract: `catalog/verification-contracts/GP-001-FHIR-verification-contract.yaml`

**Compliance Evidence:** Gate pass on PR. No collision with `GP-001` `workload_class` value confirmed by collision test.

**Lessons Learned:** The `workload_class` for a variant must be an independently unique value — the Selector does not do prefix matching.
